card.title: Haber process — why high pressure makes ammonia

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is exothermic with 4 gas moles collapsing to 2 — so high pressure (fewer moles) and low temperature (exothermic) favour yield, but low T starves the rate: industry compromises at ~450 °C, ~200 atm, iron catalyst. The same Le Chatelier logic designs Ostwald (Pt-catalysed NH₃ oxidation to HNO₃), Contact (V₂O₅, SO₂→SO₃→oleum→H₂SO₄), Solvay (NaCl + NH₃ + CO₂ → NaHCO₃) and urea (NH₃ + CO₂) plants — flow sheets included.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Haber: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, ΔH = −92 kJ/mol · ~450 °C, ~200 atm, Fe/Mo catalyst  ·  Ostwald: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ →(Pt) 4NO → NO₂ → HNO₃  ·  Contact: 2SO₂ + O₂ →(V₂O₅) 2SO₃; oleum H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄  ·  Solvay: NaCl + NH₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → NaHCO₃↓ + NH₄Cl

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Haber pressure must pay for itself (compression cost vs yield gain — the economic optimum, not the chemical maximum). Iron catalyst needs pure feed (S/CO poison it). Ostwald's Pt gauze needs ~900 °C; Contact's V₂O₅ window is ~450 °C; Solvay recycles its NH₃ (ammonia-soda loop) or the economics collapse.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Hard-water softening with washing soda: Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ precipitate as carbonates — temporary AND permanent hardness both yield (NEB 2023, 4 marks with reactions). Urea (NH₂CONH₂, 46% N) is the top-N fertiliser, made from NH₃ + CO₂. Diaphragm cells keep Cl₂ and NaOH apart to stop back-reaction.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Why high pressure for Haber? 4 gaseous moles → 2: Le Chatelier pushes right as P rises — yield climbs steeply to ~200 atm, then compression costs outrun gains (NEB 2024, 5 marks: principle + flow-sheet description + the pressure economics, plus why ~450 °C compromises rate against yield).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Single-pass conversion is only ~15% — unreacted N₂/H₂ must be recycled (flow sheet's loop). Catalysts age (poisoning, sintering). Every process pays an environmental bill: NOₓ/N₂O emissions, acidic effluent, diaphragm-cell mercury legacy (membrane cells replace it).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From equilibrium: Kp for ammonia synthesis falls with T (exothermic), so low T favours product — but Arrhenius starves the rate; the 450 °C compromise maximises rate×yield economics. Pressure: Qp vs Kp analysis shows conversion rising with P^(−2) dependence — the quantitative spine behind 'high pressure'.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Haber numbers: 450 °C, 200 atm, Fe — chant them. Every manufacture answer: principle (equilibrium/redox) + conditions + flow sheet + catalyst + uses. Hardness removal: washing soda precipitates Ca/Mg carbonates — write both reactions.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (5): Haber process + why high pressure. NEB 2023 (4): hard water — temporary/permanent removal with washing soda + reactions. Ostwald/Contact/Solvay principles with flow sheets rotate yearly.
